Nataraja (Tamil: நடராஜா, "lord of dance") is a depiction of the Hindu god Shiva as the cosmic dancer who performs his divine dance to destroy a weary universe and make preparations for the birth of a new one. The Nataraja image is one of the most well-known Hindu deities around the world. In essence, the dance of Nataraja is the dance of life, a continuous cycle of death and rebirth, creation and destruction.

The Nataraja image is typically depicted in a number of ways, but there are some common elements. Nataraja is shown with four arms. The upper right hand holds a drum, or damaru, which is said to be the sound of creation. The upper left hand holds fire, or agni, which is said to be the destroyer of the universe. The lower right hand is in the abhaya mudra, a gesture of reassurance and protection, indicating that there is no need to fear. The lower left hand points to the raised left foot, which represents liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

Nataraja is often depicted with a serpent around his neck, representing kundalini energy, and with a crescent moon on his head, representing time. He is surrounded by a ring of flames, standing on a lotus pedestal, lifting his left leg (or in rare cases, the right leg) and balancing / trampling upon a demon shown as a dwarf (Apasmara).

The Nataraja image has been depicted in various ways throughout history, with different symbolic items and variations in the posture and position of the body, fingers, ankles, neck, face, head, ear lobes, and dress.
